doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Bebop, band changes and the road
title: Hearing bebop live before records
summary: He first heard bebop live after the war, having only heard Bird's solo on a Jay McShann record, and a new crowd of players including Howard McGhee, Roy Porter and Sonny Criss.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: So when you got out of the army you came back to LA and the guys that you knew, the be bop was already being played or was it just on the recordings?
No, no, it was being played.
So you heard be bop.
Yeah.
You didn’t hear it before on any of the records? You didn’t hear Salt Peanuts, you didn’t hear (Unintelligible), you didn’t hear Ko-Ko?
I heard that after I came out of the service.
So the first be bop you heard was live so you didn’t hear the recordings of Mac -­
The first record I heard, Bird, was with, what’s his name?
Jay McShann, Tailor ( Hootie or Dexter Blues? ) Blues.

Jay McShann. There was a tenor player that used to play with him, T.J. Krump (?) was in the band, got drafted and they sent him there and he brought the record with him and Bird’s solo was on there and he used to tell us about Bird and that was it. That was it until I came home and heard all these guys, man it was -­
So Howard McGhee, and Roy Porter -- Dexter I guess was still around when you got out of the army.
No, Dexter -­
He hadn’t gone with Louis Armstrong that early had he?
Yeah, Dexter was in the east at that time.
He already left, okay. So when you came back in LA, the guys you knew were playing be-bop.
Yeah.
Now you’d been gone three or four years.
Not my cronies. I mean not the guys I came up with. This is a whole group of whole new players.
So Howard McGhee.
Yeah, McGhee.
Roy Porter. I’m just thinking of all the guys that you were hanging out with.
Sonny Criss.
Sonny Criss. Were hanging out with Bird when he came out.
Yeah, you know, all those guys.
